For q_K equal to 10 raised to K!+K, the two coordinates clear all terms through K and have first tail exponents M1=K K!-K and M2=K K!+1 with geometric tail factor at most 10/9. For T between q_K and q_(K+1), the worst-case inequality M1-log10(10/9) >= (3/5)((K+1)!+K+1) holds at K=4 and grows thereafter, proving the stated uniform 3/5 bound from 10 to the 28 onward. The rational-independence dominance argument is valid, and the stated exponential-time balancing gives the Dani first-minimum upper rate with exponent -1/16.
